name: Brass-Era Car
region: Germany, France, Britain and the United States
summary: The first motor cars. A tall, upright carriage body on wood-spoke wheels, with open seats, a folding hood, and lamps, radiator and horn of polished brass.

philosophy.core_thesis: The first car is a carriage that has lost its horse. It keeps the wood, the leather and the brass of the coach. It shows its engine as a proud machine.
design_principles: Set the body high on the chassis, with the seat 90 to 110 cm above the road.
Build the body on an ash frame, and clad it in thin sheet metal or in wood panels.
Fit wood-spoke wheels, 12 to 16 spokes each, with a thin rim and a narrow tyre.
Polish the lamps, the radiator shell, the horn and the door handles in brass, and keep them bright.
Fix the hood as a folding canvas frame on iron bows, with leather straps.
Stuff the seats deep with horsehair, and button the leather in a diamond pattern.
Leave the engine, the chain or shaft and the springs in view.
anti_patterns: Chrome plate on the lamps and the bumpers
Low, wide, closed bodies with a boot
Thick balloon tyres with a bright white wall

silhouette.shape: A tall, narrow box on high wheels, with an upright seat, a short bonnet and a flat floor; the body looks like a carriage.
silhouette.line: Vertical lines and a flat top; the bonnet is short and level, and the mudguard is a thin curve over each wheel.
silhouette.fit: Open to the weather: two rows of seats, a folding hood and a windscreen that folds flat.
silhouette.proportion: Wheel diameter 80 to 100 cm; wheelbase 2.2 to 3 m; body height about 1.8 m with the hood up.
rules: Place the driver high and upright, with the hands near the chest.
Mount the lamps on brackets at the side of the windscreen, and the horn at the driver's hand.
Keep the bonnet short and straight, with the brass radiator at its front.
Curve each mudguard thinly over the wheel, with a step board below the door.

fabrics.rule: Use the materials of the coach. Use ash for the frame and wheels, thick tanned leather for the seats, canvas for the hood and brass for every bright part.

methods: thin panels beaten over a wood buck
brass lamps and radiator shell hand polished
wood wheels with iron tyre bands
construction.closures: Leather straps and brass buckles on the hood; side doors with a simple brass latch, or no door at all.
construction.details: Brass carriage lamps at the side, a bulb horn, a brass radiator cap and a plain wood dashboard with a clock and an oil gauge.

surface.pattern: Plain body colour with a hand-painted coach line in a second colour on the panels and the wheels.
surface.gloss: Coach varnish over paint at 70–90 GU; polished brass at more than 90 GU.
surface.wear: Brass tarnishes in days, and the owner polishes it again; leather cracks and darkens; the varnish crazes with age.

palette.strategy: Dark, deep carriage colours on the body, with cream or red on the wheels, and the bright gold of brass against them.

processes: hand painting and varnishing in many coats
making.scale: One car at a time in a workshop, from 1886; from 1908 the assembly line makes thousands of the same plain model.
making.signs: Visible wood grain on the wheels, riveted brass, hand-painted coach lines and a body that leaves the chassis open to view.

pieces.form: Open two-seat body with a high bench seat and a folding hood
Brass headlamps, radiator shell and horn, polished each week
Artillery wheel with wood spokes and a thin rim
Deep-buttoned bench seat in thick leather over horsehair
Flat wood board with a brass clock and an oil sight glass

lineage.root: It is the first car style. Its parent is the horse carriage, which this data does not hold as a style.

emotion.target_response: A sense of the first journeys: adventure, noise and polished metal, a machine that people still see as a wonder.

use_cases: a period film or play set before 1915
a museum label or a rally brochure for veteran cars
an image prompt for an early motor scene
a toy or a model of an early car
avoid_when: the brief wants a closed, comfortable saloon
the brief wants a car after 1920
the brief needs a modern safe cabin

modifiers.how: Lengthen the bonnet, close the cabin with a hand-built coachwork body, and add walnut and cloth to the cabin.
Round the front, merge the mudguards into the body, and replace brass with chrome.

ornament_level.note: Plain body, rich brass; the coach line and the gilt crest are the only paint ornament.
